review: Intensive second review from source and isolated recording harnesses

samples.justification: RPS API exploit chain: bind upload evidence; fix path/session FPs
JSP command webshell: detect character output in HTTP responses

changes: Require same-call command-code data and traversal headers for requests, same-command server-page file uploads and traversal for curl, or a urllib PUT carrying read data and traversal headers alongside server-page file opening and urlopen. A web-root traversal is required for the hostile finding.
Replace unsupported admin-provisioning/dataflow names with descriptions of the fields that co-occur.
Require a session member assignment at the start of a code line; a comment ending in session. followed by admin = is insufficient.
Require a Local, LocalLow or Roaming subtree for literal Windows AppData paths; retain environment-variable paths.
Add notable PUT-body code syntax and JSP character-response output observations.
Preserve curl and urllib hostile fixtures. Update only the renamed admin-field rule ID in existing validation expectations; score and finding-count thresholds remain unchanged.

rps_chain.py: All code executes at module load. An isolated requests replacement recorded POST AddSysUser.do, POST UpdateReceivers.do, PUT rpsfile/upload, GET the JSP with cmd=whoami, then an empty PUT to the same upload destination.
The admin JSON sets FromServlet=Y, LoginName, Password and Role=admin without a prior authentication request. The receiver JSON reuses those credentials.
The upload carries a concatenated JSP request-command execution page. Its UserHome header is ../../webapps/rps and TopDir is status.jsp.
Base64 encodes the user and password for headers; it is transport encoding, not concealed code or cryptography.
The final empty PUT attempts to truncate the dropped page; it is not an HTTP DELETE. No responses are inspected. Remote exploit success is not established.
The lab description and placeholder target do not remove the executable API-abuse, traversal-write and command-execution behavior. MALICIOUS is retained for the exploit functionality.
status.jsp: The cmd HTTP parameter flows unchanged to Runtime.getRuntime().exec(cmd) under a non-null guard. There is no page-level authentication or command allowlist.
The child stdout InputStream is read byte by byte, cast to char and printed into the HTTP response; waitFor follows. Stderr is not returned.

A Java recorder replaced only Runtime capability in the extracted scriptlet. A null parameter caused no execution or output; whoami and an arbitrary command reached the recorder unchanged and returned its supplied stdout.
Runtime.exec(String) launches a program; the page does not itself explicitly invoke a shell interpreter. There is no obfuscation, outbound C2, credential theft or persistence mechanism in this page.

scope: No external conviction, advisory, scanner score or family attribution was used as proof of behavior.
